prediction_ref.short_label: Durable ask-user checkpoints become a standard harness primitive by H1 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: The June 11 prediction tracks durable, restart-surviving ask-user checkpoints becoming a standard harness primitive across multiple non-Datasette harnesses. Today's signals reinforce the long-horizon-execution substrate the primitive lives in without isolating the checkpoint itself. Huawei's HarmonyOS Agent Framework 2.0 ships an OS-level runtime for multi-step autonomous execution with a claimed task-execution success rate above 90%, the kind of long-running on-device agent loop where a durable human-checkpoint primitive would sit. More directly on the mechanism, two June arXiv papers tackle memory for long-running agents as an infrastructure concern - Infini Memory's maintainable persistent-memory architecture (64.7% on MemoryAgentBench) and Agent Memory's systems characterization with a phase-aware profiling harness - signaling that the field is hardening the state-persistence layer that a restart-durable checkpoint depends on. The divergence from the exact marker is that none of today's items ships a named, documented resumable ask-user suspension point as a generalized harness API: Huawei's is an autonomous-execution runtime and the arXiv work characterizes memory systems, so this is reinforcement of the durable-state substrate rather than a hit on the standardized ask-user checkpoint primitive.

reference_links.label: arXiv - Infini Memory: Maintainable Topic Documents for Long-Term LLM Agent Memory
Huawei Central - Huawei announces HarmonyOS 7 with smooth performance and Agentic AI upgrades

bridge.narrative: Huawei's HarmonyOS Agent Framework 2.0, with its 90%-plus on-device task-execution loop, plus the Infini Memory and Agent Memory papers treating long-horizon state persistence as infrastructure, harden exactly the durable-state layer a restart-surviving checkpoint sits on, lending the durable ask-user checkpoint thesis (Jun 11) credible substrate momentum short of the primitive itself.
bridge.remaining_gap: Need a named, documented resumable ask-user suspension point shipped as a generalized API across multiple non-Datasette harnesses, not just a maturing state-persistence substrate.

prediction_ref.short_label: US open-weights model crosses 54 on Artificial Analysis Index by Q1 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: The June 4 prediction tracks the US open-weights frontier closing the index gap to the top Chinese open model on the strength of frequent US open releases. Today's open-weights story moves the Chinese side of that race, not the US side: Moonshot published Kimi K2.7-Code, a 1-trillion-parameter open-weight Mixture-of-Experts coding model (about 32B active across 384 experts, 256K context) on Hugging Face under a Modified MIT license, reporting roughly 30% fewer reasoning tokens than K2.6 plus gains on its own suites. It sharpens the competitive backdrop the prediction is set against - a steady cadence of high-capability Chinese open releases the US frontier has to catch - but does so on the wrong side and the wrong axis: this is a Chinese release, it is coding-specialized rather than a general model carrying an Artificial Analysis Index figure, and every benchmark is self-reported with no third-party numbers on the public suites yet. No US open-weights release appears today and no AA Index score is reported, so it is weak, context-only relevance that does not advance the US-model index landing.

prediction_ref.short_label: SSM-hybrid open-weight VLMs harden into an established edge category by Q2 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: The June 12 prediction tracks the SSM-hybrid open-weight vision-language category hardening - a second Mamba/state-space-hybrid VLM family, or on-device runtime support for one. Today's news carries no signal on that axis. The day's open-weights release is Moonshot's Kimi K2.7-Code, a Mixture-of-Experts text coding model rather than a state-space-hybrid vision-language model, so it neither adds a second SSM-hybrid VLM family nor advances edge-runtime support for the architecture. Huawei's HarmonyOS 7 is an OS-level agent framework, not a vision-language model release. There is no follow-on to the Zamba2-VL line, no new Mamba-hybrid multimodal checkpoint, and no GGUF or mainstream edge-runtime support landing for the category today, so relevance is essentially nil.
